subject: Service assurance runbook for Dedicated Capacity (throughput & queueing)
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@northbridge.com>

Cc: Aaron Chu <aaron.chu@northbridge.com>
Date: Sat, 28 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated capacity — request for a service assurance runbook

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Leadership here is comfortable with the performance numbers you showed, but procurement and SRE want a concrete runbook that describes how Redwood will operate our reserved GPU pool in steady state and under stress. Specific asks from our side:

- Clear throughput guarantees (tokens/sec per reserved vGPU pool and expected variance windows)
- Exact queueing behavior and preemption/eviction rules when shared burst capacity is active
- Observability hooks we can wire into (traces/metrics + expected sampling cadence)
- Maintenance/upgrade windows and failover playbook with RTO/RPO targets

Can you send a short runbook (4–8 pages) and a simple matrix that maps SLAs to credit/remedy mechanics? We need something we can attach to the contract and to the internal risk review.

If helpful, Aaron is our SRE lead and can join a call.

Best,
Maya
VP, Platform — Northbridge Payments

(Attachment: example_sla_checklist.pdf - PDF)

From: ben_carter@redwood.com

Date: Wed, 01 Dec 2026 08:45:00 -0800
Subject: Draft: Dedicated service-assurance runbook + observability matrix (v1)

Sofia / Lauren — attaching the initial draft. High-level summary up front:

- Scope: Reserved GPU pool (8x A100-equivalent) for Northbridge — production inference only, elastic burst to shared capacity subject to preemption policy.
- SLA: 99.9% availability per calendar month for reserved pool; deterministic tail latency window defined as p99.9 token latency <= 600ms for 1–4k token requests in normal load.
- Throughput: baseline throughput target 1.2M tokens/hour per reserved pool (sustained), with 10% variance headroom; bursting allowed up to 1.6M tokens/hour in 5-minute windows subject to capacity.
- Queueing/Preemption: tenant-level inflight budget with token-bounded eviction. Preemption occurs when cluster load > 92% sustained for > 120s. Preempted requests are retried to fallback model variant or routed to burst pool depending on policy.
- Observability: provide per-tenant metrics (throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies, inflight tokens, preemptions), exported via Prometheus + tenant-scoped tracing. Default retention: 30d metrics, 90d traces (can be extended as an add-on).
- Remedies: measurement windows, credit calculus, and remediation flow (initial investigation — credit calculation — application of credit).

Attachments: 1) redwood_dedicated_service_assurance_runbook_v1.pdf (runbook) 2) nb-throughput-observability-matrix.xlsx (mapping of metrics to SLA triggers).

Questions for Sofia:
- Do we want the runbook to include example incident playbooks (eg. degraded KV cache performance) or keep them as separate operational appendices?
- Are the throughput numbers above aligned with the capacity you discussed on the call?

Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference

(Attachment: redwood_dedicated_service_assurance_runbook_v1.pdf - PDF)
(Attachment: nb-throughput-observability-matrix.xlsx - XLSX)

From: lauren_bishop@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 02 Dec 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft: Dedicated service-assurance runbook + observability matrix (v1)

Ben / Sofia — quick comments from procurement/contracting POV:

- Credits: Procurement prefers "calendar-window rolling measurement" over single-minute sampling — propose 5-minute smoothing for throughput and a 30-minute window for p99.9 to avoid noisy triggers.
- Remedy caps: cap monthly credit at 5% of subscription fee unless repeated incidents occur.
- Definition clarifications: we need explicit wording for "sustained cluster load" and how multi-tenant burst affects reserved pool latency (i.e., tie preemption to cluster-level CPU/GPU utilization metrics and inflight token counts).
- Compliance: add a short paragraph that dedicated pool observability exports do not include customer payloads and confirm what diagnostic logs will be shared during an incident.

I'll draft suggested contract language and send to both of you by EOD Friday. If Northbridge accepts the smoothing and caps, we should be in good shape for procurement to attach the runbook as an addendum.

Lauren
Enterprise Contracts — Redwood Inference
